meta.titre: Forming the comparative of short adjectives

sections.contenu_markdown: The word 'than' is a signpost: whenever you see it, a comparative form is expected right before it.

items: Spelling rule y → i before a suffix

sections.contenu_markdown: One-syllable adjectives, and two-syllable adjectives ending in -y, form their comparative by adding '-er' (changing y to i first if needed): happy → happier, tall → taller. 'Than' introduces the second term of comparison.

sections.enonce_markdown: Complete: I am really ... than I can say (happy).

etapes.justification: happy is a short adjective ending in y.

sections.conclusion_markdown: I am really happier than I can say.

items.pourquoi_faux: Short adjectives (one or two syllables ending in -y) use the -er suffix, not 'more + adjective', which is reserved for longer adjectives.
items.correction_markdown: Use -er for short adjectives, 'more' only for adjectives of three or more syllables (or certain two-syllable ones not ending in -y).

items_markdown: 'Than' signals a comparative form is needed
Short adjectives: add -er (y → i if needed)
